training.backend: CPU worlds, synchronous single-GPU native PPO

selection.rule: Per family and training seed: highest full-mission arrival count across curricula 1 and 2, then fewer contact decisions, then fewer steps. Evaluate each assembled family set together; deploy the highest macro family arrival rate. No final-test data used for selection.

policies.training: five independent PPO learners in shared worlds

validation.terrain: 256 native/WASM seeds, 48 same-settings diversity worlds, mountain/tunnel/bridge geometry, winding and lighting checks passed.
validation.browser_commands: Selection, group movement, invalid destination, momentum preservation, sensor equipment/overlays, outside release and twelve active units passed in Chrome.
validation.endurance_summary: Chrome endurance: 604.0 simulated seconds in 620.9 wall seconds; 0 runtime/GL errors, 2 stopped aircraft after impact, 6 other units moved less than one world unit during the last minute.

limitations: The 95% full-mission arrival target was not met in any family by the deployed set on the final maps.
Ground and boat arrivals improved over the route tracker in this test; quadcopter, fixed-wing and submarine arrivals did not. Learned overrides are not uniformly better than the baseline.
Narrow-passage deadlocks, route-tracking failures and aircraft impacts still occur. Group commands do not reserve space or coordinate formations.
Route localization and odometry are ideal. Cosmetic trees and rocks do not collide with vehicles or occlude sensors.
Bounded flight search can reject feasible requests. Zero unavailable routes in this test does not establish planner completeness.
Mission evaluation starts from prepared scenarios; indefinite browser patrols and arbitrary user commands are a broader distribution.
